transport: USB to RS-485, RJ45 at the controller end, 1.5 m. No protocol of its own.
gotchas: Already ruled out in docs/HARDWARE.md and the reason stands: it uses an Exar XR21B1411 with no mainline Linux driver. The in-tree `vizzini` driver was removed; what remains is an out-of-tree DKMS module that must rebuild on every kernel update and takes the charge controller offline when it does not. Disqualifying on a
A `-B` revision exists. docs/HARDWARE.md says assume nothing about its chip without checking — that check has still not been done.

The repo's standing recommendation is an isolated adapter with a mainline chip plus a hand-crimped Cat5e carrying only A, B and ground, which also removes the shared +5 V hazard between two EPEver devices by construction.
